instructions:
Determine what the supplied target does within the parent's assigned question, scope and constraints. Start with the supplied sequence, selected file contents or snippets, preserving their boundaries, completeness and known context. No initial candidate annotation or publicly searchable name is required. Possible functions can emerge from the evidence and be compared or revised. Apply the complete selected investigation instructions and thought-pattern guidance on every decision. Use actual outcomes and received child results to choose and revise your approach. Selected instructions describe how to investigate; they are not evidence about this target. Preserve the measured subject, conditions, controls, native measurements, uncertainty and limits of inference when interpreting evidence. Missing information remains unknown.

Choose an available tool action, commit a scientific interpretation through the reasoning action, commission a scoped child with its own typed return form, or wait for selected pending work when that informs the investigation. Use only the selected actual tools and their supplied resource instructions; choose callable operands through the declared response contract. Preserve the parent's exact requested result meanings and allowed values. Recorded facts come from actual records. Keep inherited information distinct from new findings and completed work distinct from attempts. Return valid partial findings and specific failures through the requested form.

Keep the assigned evidence axis, thought pattern and selected tools for this episode. process.revise prepares a different thought pattern and/or tool selection for a new child; it does not change this episode or start that child. To commission that alternative, copy its selection and revision_origin into a separately selected child assignment with the child's job, scope, constraints and typed return. Children own their iterative choices. The configured controller owns continuation. Waiting and unchanged observations do not manufacture progress. Tool-specific and resource instructions are available through knowledge.search, knowledge.entry and knowledge.read. The tool_knowledge context identifies the run-frozen library. Retrieve sections when useful; these instructions do not select work, supply scientific evidence or add execution capabilities. Use the actual tool schemas and caller-owned configuration for execution. Knowledge reads use line coordinates, not scientific source-byte anchors. No manual read is mandatory. Launch software/resource instructions have their own run-frozen library: launch.instructions.search, launch.instructions.entry, launch.instructions.read and launch.instructions.select. The launch_instruction_library context gives its identity. Select any relevant sections from one or several entries; pass the returned selection as launch_instructions in the child assignment. selected_launch_instructions contains exact sections already selected for this assignment. Instructions describe ways to work; they do not select resources, enable tools, override caller constraints, establish current availability or supply scientific evidence. Inventory and fresh observations remain separate. No instruction read or selection is mandatory.

evidence_axis.investigation_instructions:
Determine which biochemical functions are consistent with the chemistry, pathway relationships and molecular resources relevant to the supplied gene or protein. Start from the supplied sequence, selected file record or region, or snippets; no candidate annotation or searchable public name is required. Let evidence identify possible reactions or pathway roles, and preserve what is unresolved when the available material does not yet specify a chemical conversion.

For a reaction or route under consideration, identify actual reactants and products, stoichiometry, cofactors, donors and acceptors, and the boundary of any coupled system. Keep experimentally identified species and measured amounts distinct from assumed intermediates or model inputs. Consider alternative reaction orders, carrier forms or coupled steps when they explain observed products or resolve a specific inconsistency; do not fill missing chemistry with an invented route.

Where a proposed route depends on other genes or enzymes, examine evidence identifying the substrate-producing steps, downstream consumers, cofactor-regeneration steps or other needed conversions. Retain their actual identities and supporting sequence, structural or experimental measurements, distinguishing inferred annotations from experimentally characterized activities. Use those relationships to assess whether the chemical route is supported in the system being examined. A complete-looking annotation list does not establish a working pathway, and a missing annotation does not establish an absent step; preserve alternative enzymes, routes and unresolved steps.

Where the inputs permit it, examine conservation of atoms and charge under the stated species and protonation conventions, electron equivalents transferred between named donors and acceptors, and consumption versus regeneration of required carriers. Distinguish catalytic cofactors from consumed substrates. An isolated apparent activity does not establish a sustainable cycle, and an unassigned donor, acceptor or regeneration step remains unknown rather than a measured imbalance.

Retain native stoichiometries, amounts, concentrations, rate or energy units, conditions, uncertainties and the source of each measured or calculated quantity. Preserve analytical recovery limits and the difference between an observed ratio and an extrapolated fully coupled ratio. For energetic comparisons, retain temperature, concentrations or activities, standard-state conventions and assumptions. A favorable standard-state estimate is not intracellular free energy or observed flux.

Use the account to constrain the possible function without equating feasibility with demonstrated target activity or physiological use. A genuine atom, charge, electron or conditional energy contradiction can challenge a specified route; missing inputs cannot. Keep the chemical/pathway account separate from organism or sample plausibility, and preserve alternative mechanisms or system boundaries that the evidence has not distinguished.
evidence_axis.name: Biochemical feasibility and chemical/resource accounting

thought_pattern.boundary: The episode chooses the biological reaction boundary and missing coupled chemistry; a calculator only evaluates the selected account. P06 asks who supplies the output, P07 asks what rescue restores, and P11 asks whether a feasible account is used. Standard-potential feasibility is not measured cellular free energy or native flux; no credit weight is supplied.
decision_guidance: Choose the boundary and track relevant atoms/electrons/cofactors before calculating.
Kinetic activation does not supply missing thermodynamic driving force.
Keep measured balances distinct from ideal fully coupled ratios and preserve unknown potentials/recovery.
Use route-specific demands to identify which biological comparison distinguishes apparent output equivalence.
thought_pattern.description: Choose an explicit account of matter, electrons, cofactors and energy needed for a conversion. Reopen incomplete boundaries when an isolated reaction is implausible or replacement changes metabolic demand.
live_alternatives: A consumed partner or favorable coupled reaction is missing.
Partial uncoupling or another conversion alters the account.
Same output hides changed input/cofactor recycling demand.
Chemistry remains unsupported under stated assumptions.
thought_pattern.name: Account for the coupled chemical system

outcome_contingencies.if_observed: A coupled account resolves the isolated energy deficit
outcome_contingencies.then_consider: Retain feasibility under assumptions; occurrence requires separate evidence (P11).

outcome_contingencies.if_observed: Measured ratio differs from the ideal
outcome_contingencies.then_consider: Preserve measurement and consider uncoupling/incomplete recovery.
Expose the changed demand instead of asserting full interchangeability.

thought_pattern.use_when: Output conflicts with a redox/stoichiometric account, or routes with the same product may require different support.

TASK

Determine what the supplied target does within the parent's assigned question, scope and constraints. Start with the supplied sequence, selected file contents or snippets, preserving their boundaries, completeness and known context. No initial candidate annotation or publicly searchable name is required. Possible functions can emerge from the evidence and be compared or revised. Apply the complete selected investigation instructions and thought-pattern guidance on every decision. Use actual outcomes and received child results to choose and revise your approach. Selected instructions describe how to investigate; they are not evidence about this target. Preserve the measured subject, conditions, controls, native measurements, uncertainty and limits of inference when interpreting evidence. Missing information remains unknown.

Choose an available tool action, commit a scientific interpretation through the reasoning action, commission a scoped child with its own typed return form, or wait for selected pending work when that informs the investigation. Use only the selected actual tools and their supplied resource instructions; choose callable operands through the declared response contract. Preserve the parent's exact requested result meanings and allowed values. Recorded facts come from actual records. Keep inherited information distinct from new findings and completed work distinct from attempts. Return valid partial findings and specific failures through the requested form.

Keep the assigned evidence axis, thought pattern and selected tools for this episode. process.revise prepares a different thought pattern and/or tool selection for a new child; it does not change this episode or start that child. To commission that alternative, copy its selection and revision_origin into a separately selected child assignment with the child's job, scope, constraints and typed return. Children own their iterative choices. The configured controller owns continuation. Waiting and unchanged observations do not manufacture progress. Tool-specific and resource instructions are available through knowledge.search, knowledge.entry and knowledge.read. The tool_knowledge context identifies the run-frozen library. Retrieve sections when useful; these instructions do not select work, supply scientific evidence or add execution capabilities. Use the actual tool schemas and caller-owned configuration for execution. Knowledge reads use line coordinates, not scientific source-byte anchors. No manual read is mandatory. Launch software/resource instructions have their own run-frozen library: launch.instructions.search, launch.instructions.entry, launch.instructions.read and launch.instructions.select. The launch_instruction_library context gives its identity. Select any relevant sections from one or several entries; pass the returned selection as launch_instructions in the child assignment. selected_launch_instructions contains exact sections already selected for this assignment. Instructions describe ways to work; they do not select resources, enable tools, override caller constraints, establish current availability or supply scientific evidence. Inventory and fresh observations remain separate. No instruction read or selection is mandatory.

Investigate the supplied target: Biochemical feasibility and chemical/resource accounting

Determine which biochemical functions are consistent with the chemistry, pathway relationships and molecular resources relevant to the supplied gene or protein. Start from the supplied sequence, selected file record or region, or snippets; no candidate annotation or searchable public name is required. Let evidence identify possible reactions or pathway roles, and preserve what is unresolved when the available material does not yet specify a chemical conversion.

For a reaction or route under consideration, identify actual reactants and products, stoichiometry, cofactors, donors and acceptors, and the boundary of any coupled system. Keep experimentally identified species and measured amounts distinct from assumed intermediates or model inputs. Consider alternative reaction orders, carrier forms or coupled steps when they explain observed products or resolve a specific inconsistency; do not fill missing chemistry with an invented route.

Where a proposed route depends on other genes or enzymes, examine evidence identifying the substrate-producing steps, downstream consumers, cofactor-regeneration steps or other needed conversions. Retain their actual identities and supporting sequence, structural or experimental measurements, distinguishing inferred annotations from experimentally characterized activities. Use those relationships to assess whether the chemical route is supported in the system being examined. A complete-looking annotation list does not establish a working pathway, and a missing annotation does not establish an absent step; preserve alternative enzymes, routes and unresolved steps.

Where the inputs permit it, examine conservation of atoms and charge under the stated species and protonation conventions, electron equivalents transferred between named donors and acceptors, and consumption versus regeneration of required carriers. Distinguish catalytic cofactors from consumed substrates. An isolated apparent activity does not establish a sustainable cycle, and an unassigned donor, acceptor or regeneration step remains unknown rather than a measured imbalance.

Retain native stoichiometries, amounts, concentrations, rate or energy units, conditions, uncertainties and the source of each measured or calculated quantity. Preserve analytical recovery limits and the difference between an observed ratio and an extrapolated fully coupled ratio. For energetic comparisons, retain temperature, concentrations or activities, standard-state conventions and assumptions. A favorable standard-state estimate is not intracellular free energy or observed flux.

Use the account to constrain the possible function without equating feasibility with demonstrated target activity or physiological use. A genuine atom, charge, electron or conditional energy contradiction can challenge a specified route; missing inputs cannot. Keep the chemical/pathway account separate from organism or sample plausibility, and preserve alternative mechanisms or system boundaries that the evidence has not distinguished.

Reason about the evidence: Account for the coupled chemical system

Choose an explicit account of matter, electrons, cofactors and energy needed for a conversion. Reopen incomplete boundaries when an isolated reaction is implausible or replacement changes metabolic demand.

Output conflicts with a redox/stoichiometric account, or routes with the same product may require different support.

Alternatives to distinguish

- A consumed partner or favorable coupled reaction is missing.
- Partial uncoupling or another conversion alters the account.
- Same output hides changed input/cofactor recycling demand.
- Chemistry remains unsupported under stated assumptions.

How to choose and revise the investigation

- Choose the boundary and track relevant atoms/electrons/cofactors before calculating.
- Kinetic activation does not supply missing thermodynamic driving force.
- Keep measured balances distinct from ideal fully coupled ratios and preserve unknown potentials/recovery.
- Use route-specific demands to identify which biological comparison distinguishes apparent output equivalence.

How outcomes affect the next choice

| If observed | Then consider |
| --- | --- |
| A coupled account resolves the isolated energy deficit | Retain feasibility under assumptions; occurrence requires separate evidence (P11). |
| Measured ratio differs from the ideal | Preserve measurement and consider uncoupling/incomplete recovery. |
| Replacement changes a recycled product/cofactor | Expose the changed demand instead of asserting full interchangeability. |

Limits of this reasoning approach

The episode chooses the biological reaction boundary and missing coupled chemistry; a calculator only evaluates the selected account. P06 asks who supplies the output, P07 asks what rescue restores, and P11 asks whether a feasible account is used. Standard-potential feasibility is not measured cellular free energy or native flux; no credit weight is supplied.

Selected tool: perform_flux_balance_analysis (local)

Test a supplied metabolic model with selected reaction bounds or objective, returning the requested objective value or reaction fluxes.

Use the assigned question and model, together with any supplied hypothesis, evidence and reaction correspondence. For an assigned reaction knockout, set both bounds of that existing model reaction to zero. Select SBML or COBRA JSON input, optional bounds for existing reactions, and either the model's objective or one existing reaction as objective. Objective direction is retained. Describe an objective as growth only when the supplied model/question identifies it as growth or biomass. Return requested objective values or named reaction fluxes with relevant conditions and diagnostic qualifications through the existing FBA result forms and calculators. Predictions remain conditional on the supplied model and correspondence. Saved-sheet recalculation changes supported diagnostics/projections; changed models, bounds, or objectives require new selected native work.
